title: The orchestrator records an operator's gate answer on a worker branch by a documented route
goal: kb-sprint run step 4.1 and kb/_self/backlog.md Running a sprint say how the orchestrator records an answer the operator gave in its session to a gate that exists only on a worker's work/<id> branch (the command run against the worker's worktree, backlog.py --root <worktree> answer ID GATE --by operator, and the commit there), and kb-worker.md says a worker does not sign by operator for a relayed answer and hands the gate back. Answers the SP-gkbtjjce retrospective: BG-qqdfqx2d's worker refused to sign a relayed operator answer, and the orchestrator recorded it in the worker's worktree with no rule naming that route.
notes: The check passes before the work: the change is rule text; planning gives it a tested rule question in set kb-sprint:run (as ST-cjizqzhq did) as its check.
